definition: A method where exposure and readout are performed sequentially at different times for different positions on the sensor, which can cause distortion during fast movement.
example: Check for rolling shutter distortion where vertical lines bend during fast pans.

definition: A method that captures an image by aligning the exposure timing across the entire sensor.
example: Check whether the camera you will use for fast-action shoots supports a global shutter.

definition: A method of synchronizing the frame timing of multiple video devices to a reference signal.
example: In multi-camera shoots, distinguish and configure the roles of genlock and timecode.

definition: A method of setting one device's timecode onto another device and letting each device run in sync.
example: After jam-syncing the camera and the audio recorder, recheck for drift during long takes.

definition: A method of shooting at a higher frame rate than the playback standard to show motion in slow motion.
example: Shoot water splashes with overcrank and secure the necessary amount of light.

definition: A method of shooting at a lower frame rate than the playback standard to show motion sped up.
example: Use undercrank to speed up the movement of a crowd.

definition: An effect that gradually or deliberately changes the playback speed within a single clip.
example: Set the speed ramp section to match the emphasis point of the action.

definition: A technique that estimates motion between consecutive frames. It is used for video interpolation and speed conversion.
example: After applying optical flow, check whether the edges of the fingers break up.

definition: The action of cropping off part of the edge of a display, or the term for the margin area that accounts for this.
example: When placing broadcast subtitles, check the overscan and the safe area.

definition: The range of bright and dark that a camera can record or a display can reproduce.
example: Check whether the highlights outside the window and the shadows indoors fall within the dynamic range.

definition: A method of storing color-difference information at a lower resolution than the luminance information of a video, and the notation for that ratio.
example: For footage intended for chroma-key compositing, check the chroma subsampling together with the bit depth.

definition: The number of bits used to represent the value of one component of a signal. It relates to how many levels of values can be represented.
example: Before applying heavy color grading, check the bit depth of the source.

definition: A phenomenon where a gradation of brightness or color that should be smooth appears broken up into bands.
example: Check the delivery file to ensure no banding appears in the sky gradient.

definition: A workflow where an editing project is sent to another tool such as color grading or sound, and the result is reconnected back to the original work.
example: Before a color-grading round trip, align the frame rate and the file names.

definition: A used copy linked to a master component. It inherits structural or style changes from the master while some properties can be changed separately.
example: Change only the text of the button instance while keeping the shared style link.

definition: A rule that determines how a child element's position and size respond when the parent frame's size changes.
example: Set constraints so the button stays pinned to the right even as the screen width grows.

definition: Specifying text, images, or properties differently from the master in a component instance.
example: Check whether the instance's overrides are preserved after the master is updated.

definition: Breaking the link between a component instance and its master, turning it into an independent element.
example: First consider whether to detach only the special screen or to add more master variants.

definition: A composition method of placing other components or layouts inside a component or layout.
example: Nest the button inside the card to easily apply shared changes.

definition: A design token that expresses its purpose or role by name rather than the actual color or size value.
example: For an error message color, use a semantic token meaning error instead of a red value.

definition: Aligning so that it feels right to people, considering not only the coordinate center but also the shape and visual weight.
example: Finely adjust a circular icon and text using optical alignment.

definition: A typeface design or variable axis that adjusts strokes, spacing, and details to match the size at which the text is used.
example: Apply an optical size suited to that size for small body text.

definition: A font that can continuously vary the values of supported axes such as weight and width within a single font file.
example: Check the weight axis range of the variable font and apply it to headings and body text.

definition: The part of a letter that extends below the baseline.
example: Check the text area so the descenders of lowercase letters are not clipped.

definition: The reference height of capital letters in a typeface.
example: When mixing different fonts, match their sizes based on cap height.

definition: A logo combination that binds the symbol, wordmark, tagline, and so on in a fixed relationship.
example: Mark the minimum clear space of the horizontal logo lockup in the guidelines.

definition: A logo built around the lettering of a brand name.
example: Refine the letter spacing of the wordmark so it stays legible even at small sizes.

definition: A mark centered on a shape or image created to identify a brand.
example: Check whether the symbol remains recognizable in a single color and at small sizes.

definition: A visual system that consistently defines the shape, lines, meaning, and usage rules of icons.
example: Align the line weight and corner rules in the iconography guide.

definition: A formal or managed request to change the agreed scope, requirements, schedule, and so on.
example: Record the cost and schedule impact together in the change request.

definition: A document that organizes the scope of work, deliverables, schedule, and responsibilities to be performed in a contract or project.
example: Separate the number of revisions and the excluded work in the SOW.

definition: A chart that marks responsibility for each task by dividing it into responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed.
example: Check the accountable owner in the RACI so no approval is missed.

definition: A method of defining decision-making roles by distinguishing driver, approver, contributor, and informed.
example: Define the DACI for the new policy to clarify who makes the final call.

definition: The main contact person who gathers work inquiries and coordination.
example: Designate a point of contact for this matter so client inquiries are received in one place.

definition: A deadline expression meaning the end of the workday. It is best used after agreeing on the time zone and the actual time.
example: First align with the overseas contact on which time zone EOD refers to.

definition: A deadline expression meaning the end of the given work week.
example: Instead of saying you will deliver by EOW, confirm what time on Friday.

definition: Ordinary day-to-day work or a normal operating state, as distinguished from project-based change work.
example: Assign a separate person to handle BAU inquiries even during the transition work.

definition: A training method of learning the necessary knowledge and skills while performing actual work.
example: In OJT, define the tasks to be tried hands-on and the criteria for checking them.

definition: The initial reception process of receiving a work request and organizing its content, priority, and assignment.
example: Please write the purpose of the request and the needed date on the intake form.

definition: A figurative work expression meaning that the parties have mutually confirmed and agreed on handover conditions, roles, or scope.
example: We have completed the handshake with the operations team on the incident-response scope.

definition: The attitude of taking responsibility for the outcome of something and managing it to the end, or the attribution of responsibility.
example: Even for a joint task, decide who will take final ownership.

definition: A practical expression meaning to identify the cause of remaining open items or balances and settle them with appropriate accounting treatment. It does not mean erasing amounts without basis.
example: We decided to clear the books on the old suspense receipts after verifying the deposit records.

definition: Recognizing an expense in a later period. It is not a simple performance adjustment but requires an attribution judgment that meets the applicable criteria.
example: Check the expense deferral for the portion of prepaid insurance that belongs to the next period.

definition: An expression meaning to reflect sales in the accounts in line with the revenue recognition criteria and the attribution timing of a transaction.
example: Review whether a case for which inspection is not yet complete can be booked as this month's revenue.

definition: Entrusting the work of recording transactions and keeping the books to an external accounting or tax service.
example: Even when bookkeeping is outsourced, the company must accurately provide the supporting documents and transaction details.

definition: An expression meaning to approve a position to hire for, or to open it so hiring can begin.
example: We decided to open the headcount slot for the replacement hire after confirming the budget.

definition: An expression meaning that a proposal containing the employment terms is delivered to a candidate.
example: Once the compensation is approved, the offer goes out to the candidate.

definition: An expression meaning to adjust salary terms within the company's compensation standards for the relevant job, grade, and experience.
example: Review internal equity and align the offer amount to the salary table.

definition: An expression meaning to coordinate employment terms such as pay, grade, and benefits between the company's standards and the candidate's expectations.
example: Separate base pay and incentives to align the compensation package.

definition: An expression meaning to refine the wording, structure, and tone of a draft into a state that is easy to deliver. It is a different context from greenwashing, which means deceptive promotion.
example: Before sending it to the client, polish the copy by toning down exaggerated expressions.

definition: An expression meaning to structure and write the pages of a presentation deck for a report or proposal.
example: Build the pitch deck slides based on the agreed strategy.

definition: A colloquial expression meaning to actually spend the advertising budget on media placement.
example: Before burning budget on new creative, check that conversion tracking is working.

definition: An expression meaning to place ad creative on media or to run multiple creatives in rotation.
example: Fatigue has risen, so run new creative with a small budget to test it.

definition: An alternative made in a different direction from the current proposal.
example: Keep the message but also prepare an alternate option with a different style of expression.

definition: An expression meaning to rewrite advertising copy or refine it multiple times.
example: Rework the headline copy so the product's advantages become clear.

definition: The work of condensing a campaign's core logic or message into a short single sentence.
example: Before writing the opening of the proposal, summarize the value the consumer gets in one line.

definition: Presenting a different method or condition that better fits the goal, rather than simply carrying out the client's request as-is.
example: Counterpropose a channel with better target touchpoints than the requested medium.

definition: An expression meaning to create a new working branch from a base branch or similar.
example: For hotfixes, cut a branch from the current production version to work on it.

definition: An expression meaning to put a value or processing directly into the code. It is often used in the context of putting in a fixed value instead of a configuration.
example: Do not hardcode addresses that differ per environment; separate them into configuration.

definition: An expression meaning to add logging code so the execution state or errors can be checked.
example: Add diagnostic logging, excluding personal information, to the section that is hard to reproduce.

definition: An expression meaning to run a server program or instance so it can accept requests.
example: After spinning up the local server, check the API responses.

definition: An expression meaning to empty or reset the contents of a database. The scope of deletion must always be confirmed specifically.
example: Before wiping the test DB, confirm it is not connected to production.

definition: An expression meaning to run a read or modify request against a database or similar.
example: Before firing a query against a large table, review the execution plan.

definition: An informal expression referring to code written by hand, repeating similar processing.
example: Review whether the grunt-work code can be consolidated into a shared function.

definition: A specific numeric value written directly in code without a name that explains its meaning.
example: Replace the timeout's magic number with a constant that reveals its unit.

definition: A transaction method where a retailer or similar buys goods outright and bears the inventory and sales risk. The scope of possible returns depends on the transaction terms.
example: First confirm the defect-exchange and return terms for outright-purchase goods.

definition: A field expression for dividing the same product by color.
example: Sales of this shirt differ by color, so split the reorder quantity accordingly.

definition: An expression meaning an order or transaction of a single piece of goods, rather than a bundle or set quantity.
example: Check with the new client whether single-unit orders are possible.

definition: Combining multiple products or orders into a single package for shipping.
example: Bundle orders eligible for combined packing, but confirm the recipient and the ship date.
note: This entry means combined packing in shipping and packaging. For the processing of bonding fabrics, see 'fabric bonding.'

definition: A method of handing over a replacement item while collecting a defective item.
example: For defect swap exchanges, note the quantity and style number on the delivery slip.

definition: A field expression meaning to sew fabric with a sewing machine.
example: After checking the pocket position, stitch the topstitching.

definition: An expression meaning to undo the thread of an existing seam to take it apart, for example for alterations.
example: Before unpicking the side seam for a fit adjustment, check the seam allowance.

definition: Refers to a state where the intended subject is not in focus.
example: The eyes were out of focus in the key-line shot, so we reshot it.

definition: Refers to a state where the intended subject is precisely in focus.
example: Zoom in to check whether the eyes are in focus at the spot where the actor stops.

definition: An expression meaning the on-screen motion momentarily appears to break up due to dropped or duplicated frames or an editing-connection problem.
example: Compare the sections where frames jump in the delivery version against the original.

definition: An expression meaning to overlap or connect the audio of the preceding and following cuts to make the scene transition natural.
example: Overlap the audio of the next scene first to smooth the transition.

definition: An expression meaning to divide a single section into several short cuts for editing.
example: Split the cuts in information-heavy sections, but keep the meaning from breaking.

definition: An expression meaning to convert text from an editable state into vector outlines.
example: For print files, check the font usage terms and outline the necessary text before handing it over.

definition: An expression meaning to draw a vector path along the outline of a subject.
example: Trace a path along the outline of the logo image, then refine the curves.

definition: An expression meaning to adjust color, contrast, and image mood to fit the overall visual direction.
example: Match the tone of product photos shot on different days.

definition: An expression meaning to position a logo, text, or image at the appropriate spot in the layout.
example: After securing the top margin, place the logo.

definition: An expression meaning to create or print a design proposal for review.
example: Produce a draft suited to the vertical medium first.

definition: A state where an external file such as an image referenced by an editing file cannot be found.
example: Before handing off to the print shop, check the packaged files for broken links.

definition: A self-deprecating expression for the situation where revisions keep appearing even after something was called final.
example: Instead of final final file names, distinguish delivery versions by approval date and version number.

definition: An informal expression meaning to largely scrap an existing proposal or work and rebuild it from the direction and structure up.
example: Before overhauling the existing plan because the requirements changed, first check the impact.

definition: An expression meaning to take charge of a task or stakeholder and manage and coordinate its progress.
example: Client inquiries are handled by the designated person in charge.

definition: A figurative expression meaning to raise the pace and focus on driving work forward.
example: With the deadline near, push hard on the high-priority tasks.

definition: An abbreviation meaning that things differ by situation or case rather than being judged uniformly.
example: Contract terms are case by case, so do not finalize based only on past cases.

definition: An informal abbreviation meaning that preferences, methods, and reactions differ from person to person.
example: Do not brush off reporting style as person by person; set a team standard.

definition: A term for a group chat space created to exchange work announcements and materials.
example: Do not leave the final materials only in the shared chat room; also keep them in the shared repository.

definition: A critical expression used when someone feels that leftover or difficult tasks are being offloaded onto others.
example: Complaints about repeated dumping of grunt work came up, so we re-discussed the division of duties.

definition: A colloquial expression meaning to modify or get involved in part of existing work.
example: When touching an approved part, record the reason for the change.

definition: The activity of explaining and communicating a company's performance, strategy, and financial information to investors and others.
example: Explain the adjusted metrics in the IR materials by tying them to the disclosed figures.

definition: The work of estimating the economic value of a company or asset with a defined method and assumptions.
example: Specify the comparable companies and the discount rate used in the valuation.

definition: A multiple of enterprise value or equity value relative to a metric such as earnings or revenue.
example: When looking at comparable-company multiples, standardize the measurement period of the metric.

definition: A valuation multiple of enterprise value divided by EBITDA. Capital expenditures and working capital needs must be considered separately.
example: In EV/EBITDA comparisons, align the excluded items of adjusted EBITDA.

definition: The process of investigating financial, legal, and business facts and risks before a decision such as an investment or acquisition.
example: In due diligence, reconcile key-customer revenue against cash collection.

definition: Due diligence that verifies the performance, financial position, and cash flows of an acquisition or investment target.
example: In FDD, distinguish normal recurring earnings from one-off items.

definition: A due-diligence and analysis perspective that evaluates the sustainability of earnings, their conversion to cash, and one-off impacts.
example: In QoE analysis, examine related-party revenue and non-recurring costs.

definition: A metric that converts recurring contract revenue, such as subscriptions, to a monthly basis. It may differ from the accounting revenue of the current month.
example: Exclude one-off setup fees from the MRR calculation.

definition: A metric that converts recurring contract revenue to an annual basis. Distinguish it from one-off revenue and its recognition timing.
example: Break down ARR growth into new contracts and expansion from existing customers.

definition: A metric that measures the retained ratio from existing customers' base revenue, reflecting churn and contraction but excluding upsell.
example: Distinguish GRR from new-customer revenue to see the stability of existing contracts.

definition: A retention ratio that reflects churn, contraction, and expansion on existing customers' base recurring revenue. New-customer revenue is excluded.
example: Analyze whether the NRR improvement is due to price increases or to greater usage.

definition: The relationship between the cost and the revenue of acquiring and serving a single unit such as a customer or order.
example: When looking at unit economics, align the scope of contribution margin and customer acquisition cost.

definition: The work of verifying the supporting documents and policies for costs spent for work and then paying and accounting for them.
example: When settling travel expenses, submit the purpose of use together with the receipts.

definition: A document that states the reason, amount, account, and supporting documents for a payment and obtains approval.
example: Check the vendor and the payment account on the expense approval form.

definition: A field in a voucher or ledger that briefly describes the transaction.
example: Write the covered payment period and the service details in the memo line.

definition: An expense account that records spending for employees' welfare and benefits.
example: Classify meal allowances and health-checkup costs as employee benefits expense per company standards.

definition: An item that gathers costs such as transportation and lodging for work travel and business trips, per the company's account standards.
example: Settle the travel and transportation expense for an overseas trip in line with the exchange rate and supporting documents.

definition: An accounting and practical expression for spending such as entertainment and hospitality to maintain business relationships. The tax-law name and the scope of deductible expenses should be checked separately.
example: Record the attendees and the business purpose in the entertainment expense settlement.

definition: An expense item that records fees paid in exchange for external services or work handling.
example: Check the classification of payment-gateway fees and advisory fees under fees paid.

definition: The amount left after subtracting spending and so on from the allocated budget. Check the basis for whether committed costs are deducted.
example: Even if there is a remaining budget, first check the unpaid purchase orders.

definition: An expression for the procedure of filing again to correct the tax amount and so on in a previous return.
example: We found an omission in the filing and are reviewing with the person in charge whether an amended return is needed.

definition: A procedure to request a reduction or correction, for defined reasons, of a tax amount that has already been filed or assessed.
example: After checking whether there was an overfiling, review the possibility of a claim for rectification.

definition: An expression that distinguishes whether a payroll item or similar is subject to taxation. Do not judge by the item name alone; check the requirements.
example: Check whether the taxable/non-taxable classification of payroll items matches the actual payment conditions.

definition: The work of settling the applicable items such as salary, deductions, and taxes for an employee who leaves during the year.
example: In the mid-year leaver settlement, separate the amount already paid from the additional amount to be paid.

definition: Processing that bonds another fabric or film onto a fabric to adjust its thickness, form, or function. Distinguish it from logistics combined packing, which bundles goods into one package.
example: To hold the bag's shape, bond a reinforcing fabric to the outer shell and check the adhesion.

definition: The first meeting to align the goals, roles, and schedule of the work to begin.
example: At the campaign kickoff, align the target, key message, and production schedule with the client.

definition: The first meeting to align the goals, roles, and schedule of the work to begin.
example: At the development kickoff, define the requirements, deployment scope, and owners.

definition: The first meeting to align the goals, roles, and schedule of the work to begin.
example: At the new-season kickoff, align the schedules of the merchandising, design, and production teams.
